## About

The cell options from the R examples, on matplotlib figures, and svg
output. The document has no lightbox, so only marked cells open in panzoom.

Jupyter leaves the `panzoom` and `lightbox` options out of the code shown
on the page (knitr shows them); the **Code** button at the top shows the
full source.

The cases below share this setup and helper:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)

def walk(ax, n=200, title=None):
    ax.plot(np.cumsum(rng.normal(size=n)))
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title)
```

## 1. `panzoom: true` {#c1 expect-open="panzoom" expect-hint="shown"}

A cell with `panzoom: true`. It opens in panzoom with the controls hint.

```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "A cell with `panzoom: true`. It opens in panzoom with the controls hint."

x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.show()
```

## 2. Cell options {#c2 expect-open="panzoom" expect-hint="hidden" expect-max-zoom="2"}

```{python}
#| panzoom:
#|   max-zoom: 2
#|   hint: false
#| fig-cap: "A cell with `max-zoom: 2` and `hint: false`. It opens in panzoom without the hint, and zooming in stops at 2."

plt.plot(x, np.cos(x))
plt.show()
```

## 3. Labeled figure {#c3 expect-open="panzoom"}

```{python}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| panzoom:
#|   description: 'Points scattered around $y = x + \varepsilon$, with a "quote"; compare @fig-sub.'
#| fig-cap: "A labeled scatter plot, $n = 100$, with a description holding math and a cross-reference to @fig-sub. It opens in panzoom with both rendered."

pts = rng.normal(size=100)
plt.scatter(pts, pts + rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=100))
plt.show()
```

## 4. Subfigures {#c4 expect-open="panzoom"}

```{python}
#| label: fig-sub
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "Two subfigures from one cell. They open in panzoom as a two-image gallery."
#| fig-subcap: ["A random walk", "A histogram"]
#| layout-ncol: 2

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
walk(ax)
plt.show()
plt.hist(rng.normal(size=500), bins=30)
plt.show()
```

## 5. Plots in a group {#c5 expect-open="panzoom"}

```{python}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: walks
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First walk, one of two plots joined by `group: walks`. They open in panzoom as a two-image gallery."
#|   - "Second walk, in the same gallery."

for i in range(2):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    walk(ax)
    plt.show()
```

## 6. Wide collage {#c6 expect-open="panzoom" expect-fit="height"}

An 8 × 0.8 inch collage. It is a strip, so it opens in panzoom at screen
height. Jupyter figures are shown at their size in inches × 96 px (Quarto
writes it on the image), not shrunk to the column as with knitr. A 25 × 2 in
collage would be 2,400 px wide on the page, cut off at the edge of the
column. This one fits.

```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "An 8 × 0.8 inch collage of 8 panels."

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 8, figsize=(8, 0.8), layout="constrained")
for ax in axes:
    walk(ax)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=4)
plt.show()
```

## 7. `panzoom: false` in a div {#c7 expect-open="nothing"}

A cell with `panzoom: false` in a `.panzoom` div. Clicking it does nothing.

::: {.panzoom}
```{python}
#| panzoom: false
#| fig-cap: "A cell with `panzoom: false` inside a `.panzoom` div. Clicking it does nothing."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(2 * x))
plt.show()
```
:::

## 8. `classes: panzoom` {#c8 expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell marked with `classes: panzoom`. It opens in panzoom.

```{python}
#| classes: panzoom
#| fig-cap: "A cell with `classes: panzoom`. It opens in panzoom."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(3 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 9. Lightbox cell option only {#c9 expect-open="glightbox"}

A cell with only `lightbox: true`. It opens in lightbox, not panzoom.

```{python}
#| lightbox: true
#| fig-cap: "A cell with only `lightbox: true`. It opens in lightbox, not panzoom."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 10. Plain cell {#c10 expect-open="nothing"}

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "A cell with no options. With no lightbox on the page, clicking it does nothing."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(5 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 11. Both options {#c11 expect-open="panzoom"}

With Jupyter, lightbox ignores `#| lightbox:` with options under it anyway,
unlike with knitr; `lightbox: true` works, as in case 9.

```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "A cell with both `panzoom` and `lightbox:` options. panzoom takes it and drops the `lightbox:` options."
#| lightbox:
#|   group: both
#|   description: "Should not reach lightbox."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(6 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 12. svg {#c12 expect-open="panzoom" expect-fit="contain" expect-format="svg"}

Jupyter saves the figure file itself, unlike knitr (svg from R is on [image
formats](e-formats.html)), and ignores a cell's `fig-format`, so the cell
switches the matplotlib output to svg itself, and back to png after.

```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "The plot from case 1, written as svg. It opens in panzoom and stays sharp when zoomed, since the viewer redraws svg at each zoom."

%config InlineBackend.figure_formats = ["svg"]
plt.plot(x, np.exp(-x / 4) * np.sin(3 * x))
plt.show()
%config InlineBackend.figure_formats = ["png"]
```
